paper.title: Algorithm 767: A Fortran 77 package for column reduction of polynomial matrices (COLRED)
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 23(1), Mar 1997, pp. 111-129; collected as TOMS Algorithm 767
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/767.gz (ACM article not read; ACM pages return 403 from this sandbox; author list is taken from the frame item, not from the article)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 767.gz (fetched by scout 2026-11-27 into /tmp/scout-767, unpacked as text, not executed)
code.note: Shell archive. Members of interest: Drivers/Dp/data (input for example 2: DP=3, MP=NP=2, tolerance 1.0D-10, the matrix P(0)..P(3)), Drivers/Dp/RES (the shipped driver output for all eleven examples), and the COLRED source under Src/. The rerun must unpack the shar, build the COLRED driver and run example 2 with the archive's data file.

claim.location: Shipped reference output Drivers/Dp/RES inside 767.gz, block 'COLRED TEST DRIVER RESULTS, EXAMPLE( 2)', section 'The column reduced polynomial matrix R(s)', entry R(0) row 1 column 1: 151.9532407 (the column reduction of P(s) of example 2 with tolerance 1.0D-10).

reference.sha256: not recorded: the shipped text is line-split from the shar; rerun should compare the member

claim.metric: R(0)(1,1), the (1,1) coefficient of the column reduced polynomial matrix R(s) = P(s) U(s) for example 2
claim.paper_value: Shipped reference output RES, example 2: 151.9532407. The paper's printed example is not read here.

tolerance.basis: The printed value has seven decimal places, so its rounding half-unit is 5e-8, a relative 3e-10 at this magnitude. That is above double-precision roundoff for a well-conditioned reduction of a 2x2 matrix. Set before any run and not to be loosened after a run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: one COLRED call on a 2x2, degree-3 polynomial matrix.
cost.data_size: None; the input is the archive's example data (a few lines).
cost.data_licence: No data. Public netlib TOMS archive.

why: COLRED computes a unimodular transform and a column reduced form by an iterative algorithm; the (1,1) coefficient depends on every step of the reduction, so a port must reproduce it to the printed precision.
